eras.note: Assumed decennial map preceding the current one; this project's data begins in 2016, so its earlier years are outside the checked range.

eras.label: current
eras.note: Same bill as the House map, same court review. All 40 Senate seats are elected together every 4 years on a cycle offset from the governor's, so the new map's first Senate use was 2024, not 2022.

redistricting.text: Kept 84% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-1; gained the rest from the old SD-3 (8%), the old SD-2 (5%), the old SD-36 (3%). Counties: gained Leavenworth (8%), Jefferson (5%); lost Pottawatomie. 2020 presidential margin R+46.9 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+48.2 on the current lines.

Kept 62% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-2; gained the rest from the old SD-3 (38%). Counties: lost Jefferson. 2020 presidential margin D+35.3 on the 2016–2020 lines → D+57.5 on the current lines.

A new footprint: only 2% of its population was in the 2016–2020 SD-3; it draws from the old SD-19 (52%), the old SD-12 (29%), the old SD-2 (17%). Counties: gained Franklin (29%), Shawnee (23%), Osage (22%); lost Leavenworth. 2020 presidential margin R+2.5 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+11.6 on the current lines.
Lines unchanged from the 2016–2020 map. Entirely in Wyandotte County.

Kept 87% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-5; gained the rest from the old SD-3 (13%). Spans Leavenworth, Wyandotte counties. 2020 presidential margin R+3.4 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+7.4 on the current lines.

Kept 95% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-6; gained the rest from the old SD-4 (4%). Spans Wyandotte, Johnson counties. 2020 presidential margin D+26.0 on the 2016–2020 lines → D+27.4 on the current lines.

Kept 93% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-7; gained the rest from the old SD-21 (7%). Entirely in Johnson County. 2020 presidential margin D+32.0 on the 2016–2020 lines → D+31.7 on the current lines.

Kept 76% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-8; gained the rest from the old SD-11 (17%), the old SD-7 (8%). Entirely in Johnson County. 2020 presidential margin D+13.2 on the 2016–2020 lines → D+18.8 on the current lines.

A new footprint: only 39% of its population was in the 2016–2020 SD-9; it draws from the old SD-3 (44%), the old SD-5 (16%), the old SD-6 (1%). Counties: gained Leavenworth (24%), Douglas (21%), Wyandotte (16%). 2020 presidential margin R+2.6 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+12.8 on the current lines.

Kept 86% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-10; gained the rest from the old SD-21 (14%). Spans Johnson, Wyandotte counties. 2020 presidential margin D+6.4 on the 2016–2020 lines → D+1.5 on the current lines.

Kept 83% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-11; gained the rest from the old SD-37 (17%). Entirely in Johnson County. 2020 presidential margin D+6.4 on the 2016–2020 lines → D+1.1 on the current lines.

Kept 60% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-12; gained the rest from the old SD-14 (28%), the old SD-37 (12%). Counties: gained Wilson (12%), Coffey (12%), Woodson (4%); lost Bourbon. 2020 presidential margin R+46.9 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+51.0 on the current lines.

Kept 94% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-13; gained the rest from the old SD-12 (6%). Spans Crawford, Cherokee, Bourbon counties. 2020 presidential margin R+35.0 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+36.7 on the current lines.

A new footprint: only 41% of its population was in the 2016–2020 SD-14; it draws from the old SD-35 (59%). Counties: gained McPherson (40%), Marion (16%), Chase (3%); lost Wilson, Coffey, Cowley, Chautauqua and 2 more. 2020 presidential margin R+55.3 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+45.0 on the current lines.

Kept 90% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-15; gained the rest from the old SD-14 (9%), the old SD-13 (2%). Counties: gained Chautauqua (5%), Elk (3%). 2020 presidential margin R+44.4 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+47.3 on the current lines.

Kept 66% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-16; gained the rest from the old SD-30 (26%), the old SD-31 (8%). Spans Sedgwick, Butler counties. 2020 presidential margin R+28.9 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+20.8 on the current lines.

Kept 85% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-17; gained the rest from the old SD-22 (8%), the old SD-35 (7%). Counties: gained Morris (7%); lost Pottawatomie, Wabaunsee. 2020 presidential margin R+15.7 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+16.0 on the current lines.

Kept 56% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-18; gained the rest from the old SD-2 (18%), the old SD-1 (16%), the old SD-17 (9%) and 1 more. Counties: gained Jefferson (20%). 2020 presidential margin R+11.2 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+30.3 on the current lines.

Kept 86% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-21; gained the rest from the old SD-10 (14%). Entirely in Johnson County. 2020 presidential margin D+15.0 on the 2016–2020 lines → D+20.6 on the current lines.

Kept 79% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-29; gained the rest from the old SD-30 (21%). Entirely in Sedgwick County. 2020 presidential margin D+41.0 on the 2016–2020 lines → D+43.0 on the current lines.

Kept 55% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-30; gained the rest from the old SD-16 (30%), the old SD-26 (13%), the old SD-32 (2%). Spans Sedgwick, Sumner counties. 2020 presidential margin D+1.4 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+14.7 on the current lines.

Kept 86% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-31; gained the rest from the old SD-29 (8%), the old SD-25 (4%), the old SD-27 (3%). Spans Sedgwick, Harvey counties. 2020 presidential margin R+25.9 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+25.5 on the current lines.

Kept 74% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-32; gained the rest from the old SD-16 (14%), the old SD-14 (12%). Counties: gained Butler (19%); lost Barber, Kingman, Comanche. 2020 presidential margin R+47.4 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+45.1 on the current lines.

Kept 78% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-33; gained the rest from the old SD-35 (20%), the old SD-32 (2%). Counties: gained Ellsworth (9%), Comanche (2%); lost Scott, Lane, Hodgeman. 2020 presidential margin R+60.4 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+57.5 on the current lines.

Kept 92% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-34; gained the rest from the old SD-32 (8%). Counties: gained Barber (6%). 2020 presidential margin R+36.7 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+39.9 on the current lines.

A new footprint: none of its population was in the 2016–2020 SD-35; it draws from the old SD-37 (34%), the old SD-8 (26%), the old SD-23 (25%) and 2 more. Counties: gained Johnson (100%); lost McPherson, Marion, Rice, Ellsworth and 3 more. 2020 presidential margin R+46.1 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+2.2 on the current lines.

Kept 89% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-36; gained the rest from the old SD-22 (11%). Counties: gained Clay (11%). 2020 presidential margin R+63.7 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+63.0 on the current lines.

A new footprint: only 43% of its population was in the 2016–2020 SD-37; it draws from the old SD-9 (52%), the old SD-23 (4%). Spans Johnson, Miami counties. 2020 presidential margin R+23.3 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+16.9 on the current lines.

Kept 93% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-38; gained the rest from the old SD-39 (5%), the old SD-33 (2%). Counties: gained Haskell (5%), Hodgeman (2%). 2020 presidential margin R+41.6 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+43.8 on the current lines.

Kept 91% of its population from the 2016–2020 SD-39; gained the rest from the old SD-33 (9%). Counties: gained Scott (7%), Lane (2%); lost Haskell. 2020 presidential margin R+45.0 on the 2016–2020 lines → R+47.7 on the current lines.
Lines unchanged from the 2016–2020 map. Spans Ellis, Thomas, Sherman, Norton and 10 more counties.
